subproblem.title: Adjoint identity for mollification: ∫ D(η⋆u)(s) = −∫ u · div(η̌⋆s) for C¹ compactly supported η
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, ℝ^P = Euclid P with Lebesgue measure, and div G := trace DG. Let η : ℝ^P → ℝ be C¹ with compact support and put η̌(z) := η(−z). Let u : ℝ^P → ℝ and s : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be integrable. Write (k ⋆ a)(x) := ∫ k(t) a(x − t) dt (Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume). Then ∫ D(η ⋆ u)(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ u(z) div(η̌ ⋆ s)(z) dz.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (η u : Euclid P → ℝ) (s : Euclid P → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 η → HasCompactSupport η → Integrable u → Integrable s → ∫ x, fderiv ℝ (convolution η u (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x (s x) = -∫ z, u z * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ (convolution (fun z => η (-z)) s (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 3(b)(i) and 3(d) of the parent proof. These are differentiation under the integral sign, the divergence formula div(φ̌_σ ⋆ g)(y) = −∫ Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dx, and the Fubini identity ∫ Du_σ(x)(g(x)) dx = −∫ ū · div(φ̌_σ ⋆ g). Here they are stated for an arbitrary C¹ compactly supported kernel η in place of φ_σ, and arbitrary integrable u, s in place of ū, g. In Simon this is the mollification computation of Ch. 2, 2.5 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 543–545).

Notation. P ∈ ℕ. ℝ^P := Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with Lebesgue measure (volume). |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm and D the Fréchet derivative (fderiv). div G(z) := trace DG(z), the LinearMap.trace of the linear map underlying fderiv. For a kernel k : ℝ^P → ℝ and a : ℝ^P → E (E = ℝ or ℝ^P), (k ⋆ a)(x) := ∫ k(t) a(x − t) dt. This is Mathlib's `convolution k a (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x` (convolution_def, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply). η̌(z) := η(−z), which is `fun z => η (-z)` in the Lean statement. All integrals are Bochner integrals over ℝ^P.

Hypotheses: η : ℝ^P → ℝ is C¹ with compact support; u : ℝ^P → ℝ and s : ℝ^P → ℝ^P are integrable. Claim: ∫ D(η ⋆ u)(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ u(z) div(η̌ ⋆ s)(z) dz.

1. Dη is continuous, compactly supported and bounded. η is C¹, so Dη is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Off the compact set tsupport η, η vanishes on an open set, so Dη = 0 there. Hence Dη has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). A continuous compactly supported function is bounded, so fix C with ‖Dη(y)‖ ≤ C for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).

2. The reflected kernel. η̌ = η ∘ (−id) is C¹, being the composition with the linear map −id (ContDiff.comp contDiff_neg). It has compact support, since tsupport η̌ = −tsupport η (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph with Homeomorph.neg). By the chain rule, Dη̌(y) = Dη(−y) ∘ (−id), i.e. Dη̌(y)h = −Dη(−y)h for all y, h (HasFDerivAt.comp with (hasFDerivAt_id y).neg, then HasFDerivAt.fderiv). As in step 1, Dη̌ is continuous with compact support.

3. Derivative of η ⋆ u. η is C¹ with compact support and u is locally integrable (being integrable). Differentiation under the integral sign therefore gives, for every x, that η ⋆ u is differentiable at x with D(η ⋆ u)(x) = (Dη ⋆ u)(x) = ∫ u(x − t) Dη(t) dt ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ). This is Mathlib's HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left; volume on Euclid P is add-left-invariant and neg-invariant. The substitution t = x − z (convolution_eq_swap) turns this into ∫ Dη(x − z) u(z) dz.

The integrand z ↦ u(z) Dη(x − z) is integrable: the convolution of the continuous compactly supported Dη with the locally integrable u exists (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left, then ConvolutionExistsAt.integrable_swap). Evaluation at the fixed vector s(x) is a continuous linear map L(ℝ^P, ℝ) → ℝ, so it commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply):
   D(η ⋆ u)(x)(s(x)) = ∫ Dη(x − z)(s(x)) u(z) dz   for every x.   (3.1)

4. Divergence of η̌ ⋆ s. Apply the reasoning of step 3 to the C¹ compactly supported kernel η̌ and the locally integrable s. For every z, D(η̌ ⋆ s)(z) = ∫ A_{z,x} dx in L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P). Here A_{z,x} is the rank-one map h ↦ (Dη̌(z − x)h) s(x) (in Mathlib, ContinuousLinearMap.precompL applied to lsmul), and x ↦ A_{z,x} is integrable.

The trace is a linear functional on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), hence continuous. So it commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm, applied to LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap of trace ∘ coercion). The trace of the rank-one map h ↦ a(h)w, for a ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ) and w ∈ ℝ^P, is a(w) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). Hence, by step 2 and −(z − x) = x − z,
   div(η̌ ⋆ s)(z) = ∫ Dη̌(z − x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ Dη(x − z)(s(x)) dx   for every z.   (4.1)

5. Fubini. Let H(x, z) := Dη(x − z)(s(x)) · u(z) on ℝ^P × ℝ^P. H is a.e.-strongly measurable for the product measure: (x, z) ↦ Dη(x − z) is continuous, s ∘ fst and u ∘ snd are a.e.-strongly measurable, and evaluation and multiplication are continuous (ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂, AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_fst, AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd, AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).

By step 1, |H(x, z)| ≤ ‖Dη(x − z)‖ |s(x)| |u(z)| ≤ C |s(x)| |u(z)|. The bound (x, z) ↦ C |s(x)| |u(z)| is integrable on the product because s and u are integrable (Integrable.mul_prod). Hence H is integrable (Integrable.mono'), and ∫_x ∫_z H(x, z) dz dx = ∫_z ∫_x H(x, z) dx dz (integral_integral_swap).

6. Conclusion. Combine (3.1), step 5, the factoring of the constant u(z) out of the inner integral (integral_const_mul) and (4.1):
   ∫ D(η ⋆ u)(x)(s(x)) dx = ∫_x ∫_z Dη(x − z)(s(x)) u(z) dz dx = ∫_z ∫_x Dη(x − z)(s(x)) u(z) dx dz = ∫_z u(z) (∫_x Dη(x − z)(s(x)) dx) dz = ∫_z u(z) (−div(η̌ ⋆ s)(z)) dz = −∫ u(z) div(η̌ ⋆ s)(z) dz (integral_neg). ∎
The case P = 0 needs no separate treatment.

- For orientation only: the even-kernel special case (η̌ = η) is the comparator-accepted Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_sp_mollifier_adjoint of another DAG branch. That declaration is not in this node's proof base and must not be cited. Its Lean text, visible via `git show ae0277d4bed94a51b60fb4c7470fe259ed625e37:GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean` (lines 463–543), follows steps 1 and 3–6.
- It adapts to the present statement in two places: replace its oddness step by the chain rule of step 2, and in the last rewrite use Dη̌(z − x) = −Dη(x − z).
- The adapted proof compiles for the exact frozen statement with only `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`. It is about 95 lines, and its axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: Dη is continuous, compactly supported and bounded by C; η̌ = η∘(−id) is C¹ with compact support and Dη̌(y) = −Dη(−y).
Differentiation under the integral sign: D(η⋆u)(x)(s(x)) = ∫ Dη(x − z)(s(x)) u(z) dz.
div(η̌⋆s)(z) = ∫ Dη̌(z − x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ Dη(x − z)(s(x)) dx, because the trace commutes with the integral and the trace of h ↦ a(h)w is a(w).
H(x,z) = Dη(x − z)(s(x))u(z) is dominated by C|s(x)||u(z)|, so Fubini applies.
Swapping the integrals and inserting the divergence formula gives −∫ u · div(η̌⋆s).

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the C¹ compact-kernel and integrability hypotheses. The reflection chain rule supplies the correct sign; continuity of trace and the rank-one trace formula justify the divergence identity. The explicit integrable bound C‖s(x)‖|u(z)| justifies Fubini. The proof is complete, independent of other children or ancestors, and covers P = 0.

subproblem.title: L¹ approximate identity: ∫⁻|ρ⋆f − f| ≤ ε for all continuous normalized kernels supported in a small ball
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure, and let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable. For every ε > 0 there is r > 0 with the following property. Let ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_r(0) (open ball), and let (ρ ⋆ f)(x) := ∫ ρ(t) f(x − t) dt (Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume). Then ∫⁻ ‖(ρ ⋆ f)(x) − f(x)‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal(ε), i.e. the [0, ∞]-valued L¹ distance between ρ ⋆ f and f is at most ε.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ), Integrable f → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ ρ : Euclid n → ℝ, Continuous ρ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ρ z) → ∫ z, ρ z = 1 → support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) r → ∫⁻ x, ‖convolution ρ f (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x - f x‖ₑ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, L¹ convergence of mollifications by L¹ contraction, the continuous compactly supported case, and density. It is stated uniformly over all continuous normalized kernels supported in a small ball. The pointwise estimate of 4(b) is taken from Mathlib's dist_convolution_le for general kernels. In Simon this is the standard mollification fact Ch. 2, 2.5 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 543–545).

Notation. n ∈ ℕ. ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure (volume), and |·| is the Euclidean norm. For a ∈ ℝ, ‖a‖ₑ ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended norm, ‖a‖ₑ = ofReal|a|. ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral. For a kernel k and a function a, (k ⋆ a)(x) := ∫ k(t) a(x − t) dt, which is Mathlib's `convolution k a (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x`. B_r(0) is the open ball, and A + B := {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}.

Import note: Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_lintegral_sub_le is in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense, which is not in the import closure of the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean. Add `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense` to Submission.lean; accepted nodes of this run already import it, and the frozen statement elaborates without it. Minkowski sums of sets need `open scoped Pointwise`, e.g. `open scoped Pointwise in` before the theorem. All other cited lemmas are in the frozen import closure.

Fix f integrable and ε > 0.

1. L¹ contraction. Claim: for every continuous k ≥ 0 with ∫k = 1 and every a.e.-strongly measurable g, ∫⁻ ‖(k ⋆ g)(x)‖ₑ dx ≤ ∫⁻ ‖g(x)‖ₑ dx.
Proof. k is integrable (integrable_of_integral_eq_one). As k ≥ 0, ∫⁻ ‖k‖ₑ = ofReal(∫k) = 1 (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). For each x, ‖(k ⋆ g)(x)‖ₑ = ‖∫ k(t) g(x − t) dt‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖k(t)‖ₑ ‖g(x − t)‖ₑ dt (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, enorm_mul). The function (x, t) ↦ ‖k(t)‖ₑ ‖g(x − t)‖ₑ is a.e.-measurable for the product measure (AEStronglyMeasurable.convolution_integrand, then enorm). Then use Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap), translation invariance ∫⁻ ‖g(x − t)‖ₑ dx = ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ (lintegral_sub_right_eq_self), and factoring out constants (lintegral_const_mul', lintegral_mul_const):
   ∫⁻_x ‖(k ⋆ g)(x)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_x ∫⁻_t ‖k(t)‖ₑ ‖g(x − t)‖ₑ = ∫⁻_t ‖k(t)‖ₑ ∫⁻_x ‖g(x − t)‖ₑ = (∫⁻ ‖k‖ₑ)(∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ) = ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ.

2. Density. Lebesgue measure on Euclid n is regular and ℝⁿ is locally compact. So Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_lintegral_sub_le, with tolerance ofReal(ε/4) ≠ 0, gives h : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is continuous, has compact support, is integrable, and satisfies ∫⁻ ‖f(x) − h(x)‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal(ε/4).

3. Choice of r. Let S := tsupport h + closedBall(0, 1). As a sum of two compact sets it is compact (IsCompact.add), hence closed, measurable and of finite measure. Put η := ε / (4(vol(S).toReal + 1)) > 0. Since h is continuous with compact support, it is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). So there is r₀ > 0 with |h(a) − h(b)| < η whenever |a − b| < r₀ (Metric.uniformContinuous_iff). Put r := min(r₀, 1) > 0.

Now let ρ be continuous with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_r(0). Then ρ has compact support, since support ρ ⊆ closedBall(0, r), which is compact.

4. The continuous compactly supported case. For every x:
 (a) |(ρ ⋆ h)(x) − h(x)| ≤ η. Indeed (ρ ⋆ h)(x) − h(x) = ∫ ρ(t)(h(x − t) − h(x)) dt. Whenever ρ(t) ≠ 0 we have |t| < r ≤ r₀, so |h(x − t) − h(x)| ≤ η, and the bound follows from ρ ≥ 0 and ∫ρ = 1. In Mathlib this is dist_convolution_le, applied with support ρ ⊆ B_r(0), ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1, h a.e.-strongly measurable, and dist(h(y), h(x)) ≤ η for y ∈ B_r(x).
 (b) If x ∉ S, then (ρ ⋆ h)(x) = 0 = h(x). If h(x) ≠ 0, then x = x + 0 ∈ tsupport h + closedBall(0, 1) = S. If (ρ ⋆ h)(x) ≠ 0, then x = a + t with h(a) ≠ 0 and ρ(t) ≠ 0 (support_convolution_subset_swap); so a ∈ tsupport h and |t| < r ≤ 1, giving x ∈ S.
Hence ‖(ρ ⋆ h)(x) − h(x)‖ₑ ≤ 1_S(x) · ofReal(η) for all x, and (lintegral_indicator_const)
   ∫⁻ ‖ρ ⋆ h − h‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(η) · vol(S) = ofReal(η · vol(S).toReal) ≤ ofReal(ε/4),
because η · vol(S).toReal = ε · vol(S).toReal / (4(vol(S).toReal + 1)) ≤ ε/4.

5. Linearity. For every x, (ρ ⋆ f)(x) − (ρ ⋆ h)(x) = (ρ ⋆ (f − h))(x). The integrals defining (ρ ⋆ f)(x) and (ρ ⋆ h)(x) exist, because ρ is continuous with compact support and f, h are locally integrable (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left). So integral_sub and linearity of t ↦ ρ(t) · (−) apply.

6. Conclusion. For every x, by step 5 and the triangle inequality,
   ‖(ρ ⋆ f)(x) − f(x)‖ₑ ≤ ‖(ρ ⋆ (f − h))(x)‖ₑ + ‖(ρ ⋆ h)(x) − h(x)‖ₑ + ‖h(x) − f(x)‖ₑ.
The first two summands are continuous in x (HasCompactSupport.continuous_convolution_left; h is continuous), hence measurable. So the lintegral of the sum is the sum of the lintegrals (lintegral_add_left'). The three terms are bounded as follows:
- first: by step 1 (with k = ρ, g = f − h) and step 2, it is ≤ ∫⁻ ‖f − h‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(ε/4);
- second: ≤ ofReal(ε/4) by step 4;
- third: it equals ∫⁻ ‖f − h‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(ε/4).
Therefore ∫⁻ ‖ρ ⋆ f − f‖ₑ ≤ 3 · ofReal(ε/4) = ofReal(3ε/4) ≤ ofReal(ε). ∎
The case n = 0 needs no separate treatment.

Formalization note: a complete Lean proof of the exact frozen statement compiles with `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`, `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense` and `open scoped Pointwise in`. It is about 150 lines, uses the lemmas named above, and has axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: L¹ contraction: ∫⁻‖ρ⋆g‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻‖g‖ₑ for continuous ρ ≥ 0 with ∫ρ = 1, by Tonelli and translation invariance.
Density: choose h continuous with compact support and ∫⁻‖f − h‖ₑ ≤ ε/4.
Uniform continuity of h gives r ≤ 1 with |ρ⋆h − h| ≤ η everywhere, and ρ⋆h − h = 0 off the compact S = tsupport h + closedBall(0,1). Hence ∫⁻‖ρ⋆h − h‖ₑ ≤ η vol(S) ≤ ε/4.
ρ⋆f − f = ρ⋆(f − h) + (ρ⋆h − h) + (h − f), and the three ε/4 bounds sum to at most ε.

audit.reason: The type exactly expresses the uniform ε–r statement with a non-vacuous extended L¹ integral. The proof chooses r before ρ, establishes contraction by Tonelli, uses compactly supported continuous density, and controls the smoothing error on a compact Minkowski sum. Pointwise convolution existence justifies linearity; the three ε/4 estimates yield the stated bound. The proof is independent and includes n = 0.

subproblem.title: Smoothing a unit field supported in Q_δ by a kernel of radius σ < δ gives an admissible C^∞ test field for Q₁
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure, Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} and Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}. Let δ, σ ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ < δ. Let ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_σ(0) (open ball). Let s : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be a.e.-strongly measurable with |s(x)| ≤ 1 for all x and s(x) = 0 for all x ∉ Q_δ. Then G := ρ ⋆ s, G(y) = ∫ ρ(t) s(y − t) dt (Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume), is C^∞, has compact support, satisfies tsupport G ⊆ Q₁, and |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (δ σ : ℝ) (ρ : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (s : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), 0 < σ → σ < δ → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ρ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ρ z) → ∫ z, ρ z = 1 → support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid (m + 1)) σ → AEStronglyMeasurable s volume → (∀ x, ‖s x‖ ≤ 1) → (∀ x, x ∉ {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} → s x = 0) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (convolution ρ s (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) ∧ HasCompactSupport (convolution ρ s (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) ∧ tsupport (convolution ρ s (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ∧ ∀ y, ‖convolution ρ s (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume y‖ ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(b) of the parent proof: the C^∞ claim of (i), the bound (ii) and the support argument (iii). Smoothing a unit field supported in Q_δ by a kernel of radius σ < δ yields an admissible test field for Q₁. Here the convolution is written in Mathlib's order, G(y) = (ρ ⋆ s)(y) = ∫ ρ(t) s(y − t) dt. The parent's g̃ = φ̌_σ ⋆ g is the case ρ = φ̌_σ, s = g.

Notation. m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate (Lean `y i`, i.e. `y.ofLp i`), |y| the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm and D the Fréchet derivative (fderiv). Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}; B_σ(0) is the open ball. div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of the linear map underlying fderiv). For a kernel k : ℝⁿ → ℝ and a : ℝⁿ → E (E = ℝ or ℝⁿ), (k ⋆ a)(x) := ∫ k(t) a(x − t) dt; this is Mathlib's `convolution k a (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x` (convolution_def, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply). Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted measure.

Hypotheses:
- 0 < σ < δ.
- ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_σ(0).
- s : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ is a.e.-strongly measurable, |s(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and s(x) = 0 for all x ∉ Q_δ.
Put G := ρ ⋆ s. Claims: (A) G is C^∞; (B) G has compact support; (C) tsupport G ⊆ Q₁; (D) |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

1. ρ has compact support and is integrable. If x ∉ closedBall(0, σ), then x ∉ B_σ(0) ⊇ support ρ, so ρ(x) = 0. closedBall(0, σ) is compact because ℝⁿ is proper, so ρ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro (isCompact_closedBall 0 σ)). Being continuous with compact support, ρ is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).

2. s is locally integrable. Every compact K ⊆ ℝⁿ has finite measure, and s is a.e.-strongly measurable with |s| ≤ 1. So s is integrable on K (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with M = 1). Since ℝⁿ is locally compact, s is locally integrable (locallyIntegrable_iff).

3. (A) Smoothness. ρ is C^∞ with compact support and s is locally integrable. Differentiation under the integral sign therefore shows G = ρ ⋆ s is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with L = lsmul ℝ ℝ and n = ⊤; volume on Euclid n is add-left-invariant and neg-invariant).

4. (D) Sup bound. Fix y. For every t, |ρ(t) s(y − t)| = ρ(t) |s(y − t)| ≤ ρ(t), since ρ(t) ≥ 0 and |s(y − t)| ≤ 1. As ρ is integrable, |G(y)| = |∫ ρ(t) s(y − t) dt| ≤ ∫ ρ(t) dt = 1 (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).

5. Support of G. Let y ∈ support G. Then y = a + t with s(a) ≠ 0 and ρ(t) ≠ 0; this is Mathlib's support_convolution_subset_swap, support(ρ ⋆ s) ⊆ support s + support ρ. (Directly: without such a decomposition the integrand t ↦ ρ(t) s(y − t) would vanish identically, giving G(y) = 0.)
- Since s(a) ≠ 0, a ∈ Q_δ, i.e. δ < a_i < 1 − δ for all i.
- Since ρ(t) ≠ 0, |t| < σ, and so |t_i| ≤ |t| < σ for each i (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
Hence δ − σ < a_i + t_i = y_i < 1 − δ + σ for all i. Therefore support G ⊆ P := {y : δ − σ ≤ y_i ≤ 1 − δ + σ for all i}.

6. P is compact and P ⊆ Q₁.
- P is the finite intersection over i of the closed sets {y : δ − σ ≤ y_i} and {y : y_i ≤ 1 − δ + σ}, because each coordinate map y ↦ y_i is continuous linear (EuclideanSpace.proj). So P is closed.
- Since σ < δ, we have 0 < δ − σ and 1 − δ + σ < 1. So every y ∈ P satisfies 0 < y_i < 1 for all i, i.e. P ⊆ Q₁.
- Q₁ is bounded: for y ∈ Q₁, |y|² = Σ_i y_i² ≤ n, so |y| ≤ √n (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq).
Thus P is closed and bounded, hence compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded).

7. (B) and (C). P is closed and contains support G, so tsupport G = closure(support G) ⊆ P (closure_minimal). Hence tsupport G ⊆ P ⊆ Q₁, which is (C). Also tsupport G is a closed subset of the compact set P, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), which is (B). ∎

If δ ≥ 1/2, then Q_δ = ∅, s ≡ 0 and G ≡ 0. Steps 1–7 cover this case without change.

Formalization note: a complete Lean proof of the exact frozen statement compiles with only `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`. It is about 70 lines, uses the lemmas named above, and has axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: ρ has compact support in closedBall(0, σ) and is integrable; s is locally integrable (measurable and bounded).
G = ρ⋆s is C^∞ by differentiation under the integral sign (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
support G ⊆ support s + support ρ ⊆ Q_δ + B_σ(0) ⊆ P := {δ − σ ≤ y_i ≤ 1 − δ + σ}, using |t_i| ≤ |t|.
P is closed and bounded, hence compact, and P ⊆ Q₁ because σ < δ. So tsupport G ⊆ P is compact and lies in Q₁.

Empty inner cubes are covered.

subproblem.title: Mollification by a kernel of radius σ < δ does not increase the variation on Q_δ: ∫_{Q_δ}‖D(ρ⋆1_{Q₁}u)‖ ≤ V
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure, Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}, and div g := trace Dg. Let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable on Q₁ and V ∈ ℝ with ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1. Let δ, σ ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ < δ, and let ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_σ(0). Then f := ρ ⋆ (1_{Q₁}u), f(x) = ∫ ρ(t) (1_{Q₁}u)(x − t) dt (Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume), satisfies ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Df(x)‖ dx ≤ V (operator norm, Bochner integral).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V δ σ : ℝ) (ρ : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → 0 < σ → σ < δ → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ρ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ρ z) → ∫ z, ρ z = 1 → support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid (m + 1)) σ → ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ‖fderiv ℝ (convolution ρ ({y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}.indicator u) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x‖ ≤ V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, the gradient bound by duality with the smoothed unit field. It is written with Mathlib's convolution order: the parent's field g̃ = φ̌_σ ⋆ g is here G = ρ̌ ⋆ s with ρ̌(z) := ρ(−z). In Simon this is the mollification fact Ch. 2, 2.5 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 543–545) as used in the proof of Ch. 2, 2.7 (lines 651–661).

Notation. m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate (Lean `y i`, i.e. `y.ofLp i`), |y| the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm and D the Fréchet derivative (fderiv). Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}; B_σ(0) is the open ball. div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of the linear map underlying fderiv). For a kernel k : ℝⁿ → ℝ and a : ℝⁿ → E (E = ℝ or ℝⁿ), (k ⋆ a)(x) := ∫ k(t) a(x − t) dt; this is Mathlib's `convolution k a (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x` (convolution_def, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply). Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted measure. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Hypotheses:
- u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integrable on Q₁, and hyp(u, V) holds.
- 0 < σ < δ.
- ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ is C^∞, ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_σ(0).
Put ū := 1_{Q₁} u and f := ρ ⋆ ū. Claim: ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Df(x)‖ dx ≤ V.

This proof uses two sibling lemmas:
- smoothed_field (Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sa_smoothed_field): if 0 < σ < δ, k : ℝⁿ → ℝ is C^∞ with k ≥ 0, ∫k = 1 and support k ⊆ B_σ(0), and s is a.e.-strongly measurable with |s| ≤ 1 and s = 0 off Q_δ, then k ⋆ s is C^∞, has compact support, has tsupport in Q₁, and has norm ≤ 1 everywhere.
- mollify_adjoint (Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sa_mollify_adjoint): if η is C¹ with compact support and u', s are integrable, then ∫ D(η ⋆ u')(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ u'(z) div(η̌ ⋆ s)(z) dz, where η̌(z) = η(−z).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) δ > σ > 0.
 (b) Q₁ and Q_δ are measurable. Each is the finite intersection over i of {y : a < y_i} ∩ {y : y_i < b}, and y ↦ y_i is continuous (EuclideanSpace.proj; measurableSet_lt).
 (c) Q_δ ⊆ Q₁, since δ > 0 gives 0 < δ < y_i and y_i < 1 − δ < 1.
 (d) vol(Q_δ) ≤ vol(Q₁) < ∞. For y ∈ Q₁, |y|² = Σ_i y_i² ≤ n (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), so Q₁ ⊆ closedBall(0, √n), which has finite measure (measure_closedBall_lt_top).
 (e) ū is integrable on ℝⁿ (integrable_indicator_iff with (b)).
 (f) ρ has compact support, because support ρ ⊆ B_σ(0) ⊆ closedBall(0, σ), which is compact (HasCompactSupport.intro). ρ is C¹, since C^∞ implies C¹ (ContDiff.of_le).

1. f is C^∞. ρ is C^∞ with compact support and ū is locally integrable, so f = ρ ⋆ ū is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). In particular Df is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv).

2. Unit field. Let w(x) := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝⁿ).symm (Df(x)) ∈ ℝⁿ, the Riesz representative (gradient) of Df(x). Then:
- ⟨w(x), h⟩ = Df(x)h for all h (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply);
- |w(x)| = ‖Df(x)‖, because toDual is a linear isometry equivalence;
- w is continuous;
- in particular Df(x)(w(x)) = ⟨w(x), w(x)⟩ = |w(x)|² (real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq).
Define s(x) := |w(x)|⁻¹ w(x) for x ∈ Q_δ, and s(x) := 0 for x ∉ Q_δ. With 0⁻¹ = 0, this also gives s(x) = 0 where w(x) = 0; in Lean, s = Q_δ.indicator (fun x => ‖w x‖⁻¹ • w x). Then:
 (a) s is Borel measurable: w is continuous and Q_δ is measurable (Measurable.indicator).
 (b) |s(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, since |w|⁻¹ |w| ∈ {0, 1}.
 (c) s(x) = 0 for x ∉ Q_δ.
 (d) s is integrable. It is the indicator of Q_δ of a measurable function bounded by 1, and vol(Q_δ) < ∞ (integrable_indicator_iff, Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).
 (e) Df(x)(s(x)) = 1_{Q_δ}(x) ‖Df(x)‖ for all x. For x ∈ Q_δ, Df(x)(|w|⁻¹ w) = |w|⁻¹ |w|² = |w| = ‖Df(x)‖; both sides are 0 if w(x) = 0. For x ∉ Q_δ, both sides are 0.

3. Reflected kernel. ρ̌(z) := ρ(−z) satisfies:
- ρ̌ is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp contDiff_neg) and ρ̌ ≥ 0;
- ∫ρ̌ = ∫ρ = 1, since Lebesgue measure is invariant under z ↦ −z (integral_neg_eq_self);
- support ρ̌ ⊆ B_σ(0): if ρ̌(z) ≠ 0 then −z ∈ support ρ, so |z| = |−z| < σ.

4. Smoothed field. Let G := ρ̌ ⋆ s, i.e. G(y) = ∫ ρ(−t) s(y − t) dt. Apply smoothed_field with m, δ, σ, the kernel ρ̌ and the field s. Its hypotheses hold by 0(a), step 3 and 2(a)–(c). So G is C^∞, has compact support, tsupport G ⊆ Q₁, and |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

5. Testing hyp(u, V). The field −G is admissible:
- it is C^∞ (ContDiff.neg) with compact support (HasCompactSupport.neg);
- tsupport(−G) = tsupport G ⊆ Q₁ (tsupport_neg);
- |−G(y)| = |G(y)| ≤ 1.
Hence ∫_{Q₁} u · div(−G) ≤ V. Now D(−G)(y) = −DG(y) (fderiv_neg) and the trace is linear (ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_neg, map_neg), so div(−G) = −div G. Therefore (integral_neg)
   −∫_{Q₁} u(y) div G(y) dy ≤ V.   (5.1)

6. Adjoint identity. Apply mollify_adjoint with P = n, η = ρ (C¹ with compact support by 0(f)), the integrable function ū (by 0(e)) and the integrable field s (by 2(d)). The reflected kernel of ρ is ρ̌, ρ̌ ⋆ s = G, and ρ ⋆ ū = f, so
   ∫ Df(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ ū(z) div G(z) dz.   (6.1)

7. Restriction to Q₁. ū(z) div G(z) = 1_{Q₁}(z) · (u(z) div G(z)), so ∫_{ℝⁿ} ū div G = ∫_{Q₁} u div G (integral_indicator with 0(b)).

8. Conclusion. Using integral_indicator (Q_δ is measurable), then 2(e), (6.1), step 7 and (5.1):
   ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Df(x)‖ dx = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{Q_δ}(x) ‖Df(x)‖ dx = ∫_{ℝⁿ} Df(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫_{ℝⁿ} ū div G = −∫_{Q₁} u div G ≤ V. ∎
